note: Source says they were accidentally asked; "as if by accident" implies pretense.
replacement: Once they had received these instructions for their governments from Xenares, Cleobulus and their friends at Lacedaemon, the Boeotians and Corinthians left. On the road home, two high officials of Argos, who had waited for them there, joined them. These sounded them out on whether the Boeotians might join the Corinthians, Eleans and Mantineans in allying with Argos. Their idea was that, once united, they could make peace or war as they chose, against Lacedaemon or any other power. The Boeotian envoys were pleased to be asked by chance to do the very thing their friends at Lacedaemon had told them to do. The two Argives saw that their proposal was welcome and went away, promising to send ambassadors to the Boeotians. When the Boeotians reached home, they reported to the Boeotarchs what had been said to them at Lacedaemon and by the Argives they had met. The Boeotarchs were pleased with the idea and took it up with all the more eagerness because of the lucky coincidence that Argos was asking for the very thing their friends at Lacedaemon wanted. Soon afterwards ambassadors came from Argos with the proposals described. The Boeotarchs approved the terms and sent the ambassadors away with a promise to send envoys to Argos to negotiate the alliance.
